newsitem.title: USA: Grossman's leaving Mass. for Ohio, Calif.
newsitem.headline: Grossman's leaving Mass. for Ohio, Calif.

text.p: Home improvement retailer Grossman's Inc, a Bay State fixture for decades, said it will move its headquarters from Canton, Massachusetts to Cincinnati, Ohio or Sacramento, Calif., the company's chief financial officer said Thursday.

Grossman's, which operates Contractor's Warehouses and Mr. 2nd's Bargain Outlets, has closed or intends to close 60 stores in the northeastern United States as part of a reorganization plan, CFO Michael Shea said.

The company, which is also considering changing its name and stock symbol, said 40 to 60 workers at its current headquarters will be affected by the move, with some being transferred to a different division and others leaving the company entirely.
"It will take about a year" for the corporate move, Shea said in a telephone interview.
Home Depot Inc "has pretty well saturated the northeast and the west," but has left the midwest open and "we're doing quite well there," Shea said.

"There has been a huge amount of growth in the midwest over the last year-and-a-half...the economy is growing. There are a lot of new houses in say Lexington, Kentucky and Ft. Wayne, Indiana where we have stores and they're doing quite well," Shea said.

Grossman's, which operates six stores in the midwest and has 1,800 workers nationwide, owns a large building in Cincinnati and "We would not have to buy any or rent any more space there for our corporate staff," Shea said. He estimated that when the move is completed, only 10 or so corporate jobs will be involved in the move.
For the third quarter, net income was $1.6 million or 5 cents a share compared with $15.3 million or 59 cents a share a year earlier.
Earnings in the 1995 period included an $18.1 million gain from the sale of its former headquarters and $4.5 million in store closing expenses.
During the first quarter of 1996, Grossman's closed 60 stores in the northeast including New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
Through the first nine months of 1996, $40 million in restructuring costs caused Grossman's to report a loss of $56.1 million or $2.11 a share.
Sales for the first nine months were $296.7 million in 1996 and $514.7 million in 1995.
